module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1138

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1138](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1138)
- [Va99] Vardi, I., Prime census. (1999).
- [Kum26] Kumrawat, S., [Disproof of Erdős Problem 1138](https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf).

Note that the conjecture has a claimed disproof found at:
https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf,
see the discussion section on the Erdos problems website for more information.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Filter Asymptotics Real Set

namespace Erdos1138

/--
The maximal prime gap below $x$, i.e. $d(x) = \max_{p_n < x}(p_{n+1} - p_n)$, where $p_n$
denotes the $n$-th prime.
-/
noncomputable def sup_primeGap (x : ℝ) : ℕ := (Finset.range (primeCounting' ⌈x⌉₊)).sup primeGap

/--
The filter on $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ corresponding to sending $x \to \infty$ subject to $x/2 < y < x$
-/
abbrev snd_gt_half_fst : Filter (ℝ × ℝ) := atTop.comap Prod.fst ⊓ 𝓟 {p | p.2 ∈ Ioo (p.1 / 2) p.1}

/-- Given a pair $(x,y)$, this is the amount of primes in the interval above $y$, of length
equalling the largest prime gap before $x$, scaled by a constant $C$.
-/
noncomputable def primeCount_Ioc_mul_const (C : ℝ) : (ℝ × ℝ) → ℝ :=
  fun (x, y) ↦ (primeCounting ⌊y + C * sup_primeGap x⌋₊ - primeCounting ⌊y⌋₊)

/--
**Erdős Problem 1138.**
Let $x/2 < y < x$ and $C > 1$. If $d = \max_{p_n < x}(p_{n+1} - p_n)$,
where $p_n$ denotes the $n$-th prime, then is it true that
$$\pi(y + Cd) - \pi(y) \sim \frac{Cd}{\log y}$$?
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/YanYablonovskiy/formal-conjectures/blob/7c134317104d3b98ecc751afbb79ec0adddf8e7c/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1138a.lean#L496"]
theorem erdos_1138 : answer(False) ↔ ∀C > 1,
    primeCount_Ioc_mul_const C ~[snd_gt_half_fst] fun (x, y) ↦
      C * (sup_primeGap x) / Real.log y := by
  sorry

end Erdos1138

findings.description: The module docstring expands the source key [Va99] as "Vardi, I., Prime census. (1999)." This is not the reference the source cites. erdosproblems.com/1138 gives its source as "[Va99,1.3]", and the site's bibliography defines [Va99] as the 1999 Budapest conference booklet. The repository's own Erdős README and other files (119, 164, 300, 1141, 1142, 1147, 1148) use that same expansion. No mathematics is affected.

Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999)." The Sunder–Kumrawat–Cheri note also gives the original source as "[2, 1.3]" with [2] = "Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems…".
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the line with: `- [Va99] Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).`

findings.description: The disproof is cited as "[Kum26] Kumrawat, S., Disproof of Erdős Problem 1138". The linked PDF has three authors (Hrishi Sunder, Sourish Kumrawat and Kireet Cheri) and is titled "An Elementary Obstruction to a Uniform Prime-Gap Asymptotic" (April 2026). The site credits "Sunder, Kumrawat, Cheri, and GPT 5.5". So the citation drops two authors and does not use the paper's title. The URL is correct and the mathematics is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: Title page of https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf: "AN ELEMENTARY OBSTRUCTION TO A UNIFORM PRIME-GAP ASYMPTOTIC — HRISHI SUNDER, SOURISH KUMRAWAT, AND KIREET CHERI", dated April 2026. erdosproblems.com/latex/1138: "This was disproved by Sunder, Kumrawat, Cheri, and GPT 5.5".
findings.suggested_fix: `- [SKC26] Sunder, H., Kumrawat, S., Cheri, K., [An elementary obstruction to a uniform prime-gap asymptotic](https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf) (2026).` Optionally add the site's solution sentence to the theorem docstring, as the Erdős README asks for solved problems.

reformulations.difference: The source says: let x/2<y<x and C>1, is π(y+Cd)−π(y) ∼ Cd/log y? The Lean states `answer(False) ↔ ∀ C > 1, f_C ~[snd_gt_half_fst] g_C`. Three things differ in form. (1) The filter is `comap Prod.fst atTop ⊓ 𝓟 {p | p.2 ∈ Ioo (p.1/2) p.1}` on ℝ×ℝ, so the asymptotic is taken uniformly in y ∈ (x/2, x) as x → ∞. (2) `~` is Mathlib's `(f−g) =o g` rather than a ratio tending to 1. (3) π(t) is written `primeCounting ⌊t⌋₊`, and primes are 0-indexed through `nth Nat.Prime`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) I proved in Lean that eventually along the filter is the same as ∃X ∀x≥X ∀y ∈ (x/2, x); the filter is also `NeBot`. By the usual choice/diagonal argument, this uniform condition is equivalent to convergence along every choice y = y(x) ∈ (x/2, x). That is the reading the site uses: its disproof takes x = p_n+1, y = p_n−2d. The solvers use the same reading and call it the standard interpretation. (2) For x > 2, d(x) ≥ 1 because p_0 = 2 has gap 1, and log y > 0 once y > 1. So g = C·d/log y > 0 eventually, and (f−g) = o(g) is equivalent to f/g → 1. That is exactly A(C) in the Sunder–Kumrawat–Cheri note. (3) For y ≥ 0, #{p ≤ y} = primeCounting ⌊y⌋₊. The maximum over all p_n < x does not depend on how primes are indexed; Lean confirms d(10)=4, d(7)=2 and d(7.5)=4. Finally, `answer(False) ↔ P` is ¬P, and ¬P is what the site and the paper establish. The linked Lean proof derives ¬P from these exact definitions.

review.notes:
No misformalization was found. `erdos_1138` states the source's question under the source's own reading: uniform in x/2<y<x, for every fixed C>1. The answer `False` matches the site's DISPROVED (LEAN) status. The category (`research solved`) and `answer(False)` are consistent with the source, so there are no status issues.

formal_proof check (per PROOFS.md): I compiled the linked `1138a.lean` (commit 7c13431…, L496 is the attribute line of `erdos1138_corollary`) against the committed `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«1138»` module. The only edit was replacing the old `FormalConjectures.Util.ProblemImports` import with `FormalConjecturesUtil`. It builds with deprecation warnings only. `#print axioms Erdos1138a.erdos1138_corollary` gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and `⟨False.elim, erdos1138_corollary⟩ : type_of% Erdos1138.erdos_1138` type-checks. The file has no `sorry`. The `formal_conjectures` kind points to a fork, which matches existing practice in the repository.

Non-mathematical observations:
- The module docstring still calls the disproof \"claimed\", but the site now lists the problem as DISPROVED (LEAN).
- The theorem docstring omits the site's solution sentence, which the Erdős README asks for on solved problems.
- The site mentions open extensions in its comments. Tao observes that the set of C for which A(C) holds is closed under addition and subtraction. The record-gap argument excludes nonzero elements of (−1,1), so either no C > 1 works or the set is a lattice LZ with L ≥ 1. Whether each individual fixed C > 1 fails is therefore open, as is the slowly growing C = C(x) regime. The file does not formalize these; they could be added as `research open` variants.
